newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Drought worsens in south and east Australia-Bureau.
newsitem.headline: Drought worsens in south and east Australia-Bureau.

text.p: Below average rainfall totals through much of southern and eastern Australia during July had resulted in a worsening of rainfall deficiencies, Bureau of Meteorology director John Zillman said on Tuesday.

For the 10 months to July 31, serious to severe deficiencies were evident along the coast and in the southeast corner of South Australia, in most of western, northern and central Victoria and in the east of Tasmania, he said in a statement.
Areas of driest on record totals expanded in July and were evident in central and western Victoria, adjacent parts of South Australia and on Flinders Island and the east coast of Tasmania.

For the shorter five-month period ended July 31, regions of serious to severe deficiencies were evident through southeast South Australia, western, northern and central Victoria, southwest and central New South Wales, pockets in southeast Queensland, central Northern Territory and southwest Western Australia, he said.
Pockets of driest on record totals were evident in southern inland South Australia and east central Victoria, he said.

Earlier, the bureau said the current strong El Nino event had produced a strong likelihood of significantly drier than normal weather persisting and expanding across much of eastern and southern Australia in the next three months.
